headline: Intel and AMD shares dropped about 4% before the market opened after Nvidia revealed its first processors for Windows PCs.
score_reason: Stale: the Computex announcement and share move appear to date from June, not this week; lowered by 2 from 6.
importance_line: PC buyers may get a new chip choice this fall and Intel and AMD face a new rival, but the share fall was a one-day premarket move and the date of the underlying news is unclear.
summary: Stocktwits reports that Intel and AMD shares fell about 4.2% in premarket trading on a Monday after Nvidia, working with Microsoft, unveiled its first PC processor, the Arm-based N1X, at the Computex show in Taipei for Windows PCs due this fall. The article refers to Computex 2026, an event held earlier in the year, so this is older news carried again; the share move is a short-term reaction and not a measure of lasting damage.
notes: Freshness date is inferred (Computex 2026 is a June event; day not stated in the article), so freshness gives month only. Score lowered for staleness.
